title: A Columbia session where the band was told not to sound good
summary: The Dick Vance band had to sound less polished for a singer's record date.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: Just to play their instruments, you know, whatever. We made -- we went to make an audition, not an audition. It was a record date at Columbia, and Mitch Miller was the director. Dick Vance was the leader with Eddy Barefield, Taft Jordan, I think. We had a good band. And Dick had written the arrangements for the actor. I can't think of his name right now. [Brock Peters]
We spent the whole session trying to make the band not sound good.
What was the purpose of that?

Well, that isn't what they wanted. But naturally, Dick is going to hire all professionals. The band sounded too good, so moving things around -- and so we asked, you know, well, you know, try to get a different sound.
